title: World outline map with rivers
subject: Geography
unit: Summer 1: Rivers and the water cycle (Flow and One Planet, Our World)
source: Written for geography/y3 lesson 15 (World outline map with rivers (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 15: Great rivers of the world. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Trace each river in blue and write its name. Which continent is each one in?

blocks.answers: Nile: Africa; Amazon: South America; Mississippi: North America; Yangtze: Asia; Ganges: Asia; Thames: Europe.

bullets: The Nile is about 6,650 km long
The Amazon carries the most water

model.title: How much longer is the Nile than the Thames?

keywords.def: one of seven very large areas of land
the world's longest river, in Africa
the river carrying the most water, in South America
two rivers in Iraq, where early cities grew

questions.q: Which continent is the Amazon in?
Which city grew on the Tigris?
Give one reason people live by rivers.
questions.a: Water, fertile soil, travel or trade

questions.q: Core: On the world map, mark and label the Nile, Amazon, Thames, Tigris and Euphrates, and write the continent beside each.
questions.a: All five rivers and continents correct

questions.q: Extend: Write a sentence comparing the Nile and the Thames.
questions.a: The Nile is much longer than the Thames: about 6,650 km compared with about 346 km.

questions.q: Stretch: Why did the first cities grow by the Tigris, Euphrates and Nile?
questions.a: Fertile soil from floods and water for farming meant enough food for many people

questions.q: The longest river in the world is the:
questions.a: B) Nile. The Nile is about 6,650 km; the Amazon is close but carries more water.

questions.q: The Tigris and Euphrates are in:
Big question: a long river or a wide one: which matters more?
questions.a: Either, with a reason: what matters most is water, soil and travel for people
